North Hertfordshire's population increased by around 6,100 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 130,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of North Hertfordshire increased by 4.8%, from around 127,100 in 2011 to around 133,200 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, North Hertfordshire was home to around 2.5 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 2.4 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 35% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in North Hertfordshire than across the East of England

An older North Hertfordshire

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of North Hertfordshire increased by two years, from 40 to 42 years of age.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 3,100 (an increase of 13.3%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 1,500 (5.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Unpaid care in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 4.9% of North Hertfordshire residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.5% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.2% in 2011. The proportion of North Hertfordshire residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.0% to 2.2%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in North Hertfordshire (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in North Hertfordshire decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 44.5% of North Hertfordshire residents reported having "No religion", making it the most common response in this local authority area (up from 30.4% in 2011). Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 43.8% of people in North Hertfordshire described themselves as Christian (down from 57.0%), while 6.0% did not state their religion (down from 7.4% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

North Hertfordshire residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 114,300 North Hertfordshire residents said they were born in England. This represented 85.8% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 110,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 86.8% of North Hertfordshire's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with just under 1,900 North Hertfordshire residents reporting this country of birth (1.4%). This figure was down from just over 2,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.7% of the population of North Hertfordshire.

The number of North Hertfordshire residents born in India remained close to 1,800 between the last two census (from 1.4% of the local population in 2011 to 1.3% in 2021)

In 2021, 85.8% of North Hertfordshire residents reported their country of birth as England

People looking after their family or home in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 3.9% of North Hertfordshire residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home. This figure was the same in 2011.

The percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home increased from 4.1% to 4.6% across the East of England. Across England, the percentage increased from 4.0% to 4.8%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

In 2021, 3.9% of usual residents aged 16 years and over said they were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home in North Hertfordshire

Working hours in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 10.3% of North Hertfordshire residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (10.2%).

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 10.4% to 10.8% across the East of England. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

In 2021, 10.3% of usual residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week in North Hertfordshire

National identity in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 6.0% of North Hertfordshire residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 5.4% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the East of England (2.1 percentage points, from 6.9% to 9.0%) than in North Hertfordshire (0.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in North Hertfordshire increased by 0.6 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

Of North Hertfordshire households, 18.0% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.6%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.4% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 6.1% to 6.5%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater across the East of England (1.8 percentage points, from 19.0% to 17.2%) than in North Hertfordshire (1.5 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in North Hertfordshire decreased by 1.5 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of North Hertfordshire residents aged 16 years and over, 33.9% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 30.2% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (48.8%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 51.4% in 2011. The percentage of adults in North Hertfordshire that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.8% to 8.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in North Hertfordshire (3.7 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the East of England (3.7 percentage points, from 31.1% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in North Hertfordshire increased by 3.7 percentage points

Change in housing in North Hertfordshire

Of North Hertfordshire households, 64.8% owned their home in 2021, down from 65.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in seven households (15.4%) rented privately, compared with 13.1% in 2011. The percentage of North Hertfordshire households that lived in a socially rented property decreased from 19.3% to 18.7%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater across the East of England (2.4 percentage points, from 67.6% to 65.2%) than in North Hertfordshire (0.8 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in North Hertfordshire decreased by 0.8 percentage points

Disability in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 5.8% of North Hertfordshire residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.6% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.1%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.3% in 2011. The proportion of North Hertfordshire residents who were not disabled decreased from 84.1% to 84.0%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the East of England (1.2 percentage points, from 7.8% to 6.6%) than in North Hertfordshire (0.8 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in North Hertfordshire decreased by 0.8 percentage points

Health in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 50.3% of North Hertfordshire residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 48.7% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.8% to 34.4%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of North Hertfordshire residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.8% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.3% to 3.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in North Hertfordshire increased by 1.6 percentage points

Ethnic groups in North Hertfordshire

In 2021, 3.7% of North Hertfordshire residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 2.7% in 2011. The 1.0 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.9% to 2.8%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 87.5% of people in North Hertfordshire identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 89.5% in 2011), while 5.2% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 5.4% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 2.0% in 2011 to 2.4% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
